newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Suspected rebels attack East Timor wedding party.
newsitem.headline: Suspected rebels attack East Timor wedding party.

text.p: An East Timorese man was killed after suspected separatist rebels stormed a wedding party, the official Antara news agency reported on Tuesday.

Antara quoted East Timor military commander Colonel Slamat Sidabutar as saying that Domingos da Silva was killed on Sunday evening while attending the wedding in Baucau, 130 km (81 miles) east of the provincial capital Dili.
"When the wedding was being held, suddenly a group of people stormed the place, which caused the death of Domingos da Silva," Sidabutar said.

He said the attackers, whom he described as Timorese rebels, killed da Silva while he was eating. There was no word on why the rebels would attack a wedding party and whether da Silva was the target of the attack.
Antara gave no further details. The military could not be reached for comment.

At least 34 people died in Timor as a result of attacks by rebels seeking to disrupt the May 29 general elections, in which Indonesia's ruling Golkar party swept 74 percent of the vote nationwide, police have said.
Indonesian security forces have so far captured 120 members of the guerrilla movement opposing Jakarta's rule in Timor following the election-related attacks.

Nine other people have also been arrested for allegedly setting fire to the largest market in Dili two weeks ago, in which at least 30 kiosks were burned. Police believe rebels were behind the incident.
Indonesia occupied the former Portuguese colony of East Timor in 1975 and annexed it the following year in a move not recognised by the United Nations.
